questions.stem: In the administration of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, the council of eight ministers that assisted him was known as the:

options.option_text: Ashtapradhan
Navratna
Dahshala
Peshwai

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Ashtapradhan was the council of eight ministers created by Shivaji to head the civil and military administration of the Maratha Empire. The most important among them was the Peshwa (Prime Minister). Unlike the later Maratha Empire where the Peshwas became hereditary rulers, under Shivaji, these positions were strictly non-hereditary and the ministers were directly accountable to him.
DECOY BUSTING: The Navratnas (Nine Gems) were the courtiers of Akbar (and Chandragupta II). Dahshala was Akbar's land revenue system devised by Todar Mal. Peshwai refers to the later era when the Peshwas took over the empire from Shivaji's descendants.
EXAM INSIGHT: Key ministers to remember: Peshwa (Prime Minister), Amatya (Finance Minister), Sumant (Foreign Minister), and Senapati (Commander-in-Chief).

questions.stem: What were 'Chauth' and 'Sardeshmukhi' in the context of the Maratha Empire?

options.option_text: They were taxes extracted by the Marathas from neighboring territories not directly under their administration, in exchange for protection from Maratha raids
They were distinct titles given to the commanders of the Maratha navy
They were two types of highly fertile agricultural lands directly owned by the Chhatrapati
They were religious taxes levied specifically on non-Hindus living within the Maratha kingdom

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: 'Chauth' was a military tribute (amounting to 1/4th of the standard land revenue) demanded by Shivaji from neighboring Mughal or Deccan Sultanate territories. Paying it ensured the Marathas would not raid your land. 'Sardeshmukhi' was an additional 10% levy that Shivaji demanded on top of the Chauth, claiming he was the supreme head (Sardeshmukh) of all the Deshmukhs (local chiefs) in Maharashtra.
DECOY BUSTING: The commander of the Maratha Navy was Kanhoji Angre (Sarkhel). Royal agricultural lands were known as 'Khalisa'. Religious tax on non-Muslims (under Mughals) was Jizya; Shivaji did not levy religious taxes on Muslims.
EXAM INSIGHT: These taxes were a massive source of income that fueled the rapid expansion of the Maratha military machine, but they also severely alienated neighboring rulers and populations, which proved fatal for the Marathas later on.

questions.stem: At which fort was Shivaji officially crowned Chhatrapati during the rajyabhishek ceremony of June 1674?

options.option_text: Rajgad Fort, which served as Shivaji's administrative capital from 1648
Raigad Fort, located in the Sahyadri range of present-day Maharashtra
Pratapgad Fort, near Mahabaleshwar and site of the famous Afzal Khan battle
Torna Fort, also known as Prachandagad, the first fort seized by Shivaji

questions.explanation: Raigad Fort in the Sahyadri range became Shivaji's capital and the site of his coronation as Chhatrapati on 6 June 1674. Rajgad was his earlier capital before Raigad; Pratapgad is famous for the 1659 Afzal Khan encounter; Torna was the first fort he captured as a teenager — none were the coronation site.

questions.stem: Which Vedic scholar performed Shivaji's rajyabhishek in 1674 and resolved the controversy surrounding his Kshatriya lineage?

options.option_text: Ramchandra Pant Amatya, the administrator who later wrote the Ajnapatra treatise
Gaga Bhatt (Vishweshwar Bhatt), a renowned Vedic scholar from Kashi (Varanasi)
Moropant Trimbak Pingle, who served as the first Peshwa under Shivaji's court
Nischal Puri Goswami, a Vaishnava saint patronized by the Maratha royal court

questions.explanation: Gaga Bhatt (Vishweshwar Bhatt) from Kashi established Shivaji's descent from the Mewar Sisodiya Rajput clan, resolving objections about his Kshatriya status and enabling full Vedic coronation rites. Ramchandra Pant Amatya was a later administrator who served under Rajaram; Moropant Pingle was Shivaji's Peshwa, not the officiant of the ceremony.

questions.stem: The Treaty of Purandar (1665) was a significant setback for Shivaji. Which combination of facts about this treaty is historically accurate?

options.option_text: Shaista Khan negotiated the pact; Shivaji surrendered 12 forts and paid war indemnity
Mirza Raja Jai Singh I negotiated the pact; Shivaji surrendered 23 out of 35 forts
Aurangzeb personally oversaw the terms; Shivaji ceded all his coastal forts to Mughals
Dilir Khan led the negotiations; Shivaji agreed to supply troops for Mughal Deccan wars

questions.explanation: Mirza Raja Jai Singh I of Amber besieged Purandar and negotiated the 1665 treaty. Shivaji surrendered 23 of his 35 forts and agreed to send his son Sambhaji to the Mughal court. Shaista Khan was the Mughal Deccan governor earlier defeated by Shivaji in 1663; he did not negotiate Purandar. Aurangzeb was not personally present.

questions.stem: Which concealed weapon did Shivaji use during his famous meeting with Bijapur general Afzal Khan at Pratapgad in 1659?

options.option_text: Katar, a triangular push-dagger widely favoured by Mughal and Deccan nobility
Bagh nakh, a claw-shaped weapon designed to fit over the closed fist
Pata, a gauntlet-style broadsword that was distinctive to Maratha warriors
Bichuwa, a wavy-bladed dagger associated with both Rajput and Maratha courts

questions.explanation: Shivaji concealed a bagh nakh — literally 'tiger's claw', a hand-worn weapon with curved iron blades — and used it to fatally wound Afzal Khan when the general attempted treachery during their embrace. The katar is a push-dagger (different weapon), the pata a gauntlet-sword, and the bichuwa a wavy dagger — none are the specific weapon used in this encounter.

questions.stem: Which sea fort did Shivaji himself construct (not merely capture) to establish Maratha naval power and challenge Portuguese dominance on the Konkan coast?

options.option_text: Janjira Fort, located off the Murud coast and controlled by the Siddis of Deccan
Sindhudurg Fort, built on a rocky islet near Malvan between 1664 and 1667
Vijaydurg Fort, regarded as the oldest standing fortification along the Konkan coast
Suvarnadurg Fort, a sea-fort situated near Harnai in the Ratnagiri coastal district

questions.explanation: Sindhudurg (1664–1667) was Shivaji's own construction on a rocky island near Malvan and became the symbol of Maratha sea power. Janjira was held by the Siddi rulers and was never captured by Shivaji despite repeated attempts — a notable failure. Vijaydurg and Suvarnadurg were pre-existing forts that Shivaji captured and expanded, not ones he built from scratch.

questions.stem: Shivaji's infantry backbone consisted of 'Mavala' soldiers. Which option most accurately describes the social and geographic origin of this fighting force?

options.option_text: Ex-Bijapur soldiers from Karnataka recruited after Shivaji's southern military campaigns
Hardy peasant warriors from the Maval valleys of the Western Ghats near Pune
Mercenary Arab and Habshi fighters hired to neutralise Mughal heavy cavalry formations
Brahmin volunteers from the Konkan coast trained in guerrilla warfare from early campaigns

questions.explanation: The Mavala (or Mavali) were peasant foot-soldiers drawn from the Maval region — a cluster of valleys along the Western Ghats near Pune, covering the Bhima, Nira, and Ghod river basins. Their intimate knowledge of the rugged Sahyadri terrain made them ideal for the guerrilla warfare that defined Shivaji's early campaigns. They were not mercenaries, Brahmins, nor ex-Bijapur troops.

questions.stem: A significant controversy before Shivaji's 1674 coronation concerned his varna classification. Which of the following best describes how this dispute was historically resolved?

options.option_text: Shivaji accepted a Tantric-style coronation, sidestepping the Brahmin varna objection
Gaga Bhatt traced Shivaji's descent to Mewar's Sisodiya Rajputs, legitimising Vedic rites
Nischal Puri Goswami performed a Vaishnava ceremony, bypassing the Brahmin-led dispute
Aurangzeb's diplomatic pressure forced Shivaji to postpone and revise the coronation format

questions.explanation: Several Brahmins initially refused to perform the sacred thread and coronation rituals, questioning Shivaji's Kshatriya lineage. Gaga Bhatt (Vishweshwar Bhatt from Kashi) resolved this by establishing a genealogical link between the Bhonsle clan and the Sisodiya Rajputs of Mewar — a recognised Kshatriya lineage — thereby legitimising the full Vedic rajyabhishek at Raigad. The tantric and Vaishnava ceremony options are fabricated; Aurangzeb had no role in the coronation format.
